title: Switch
summary: git switch (or git checkout) moves you to another branch, changing your files to match it.

levels.title: Change branches
levels.briefing: HEAD marks where you are. git switch <branch> moves HEAD to that branch and updates your files to match its latest commit. New commits are then added to that branch. git checkout <branch> does the same thing; it is the older command.
levels.objective: Switch to the existing branch called feature.

cheatsheet.description: Create a branch and move to it
Older way to move to a branch
Older way to create and move

hints: git branch shows that you are on main.
git switch takes the branch name.
levels.successMessage: HEAD moved to feature, and feature.txt appeared because it exists on that branch.

levels.title: Create and switch
levels.objective: Create a branch called login and switch to it, in one command.
hints: git switch has a flag that creates the branch first.
The flag is -c (or -b with git checkout).
levels.successMessage: Creating and switching in one step is the usual way to start new work.

levels.title: Work on a branch
levels.objective: On the feature branch, commit a file called feature.txt. Then switch back to main.
hints: Switch first, so the commit lands on feature.
Create, stage and commit the file, then switch back.
Run: git switch feature, touch feature.txt, git add feature.txt, git commit -m "Add feature", git switch main
levels.successMessage: Back on main, feature.txt is gone from your folder. It is safe on the feature branch.

levels.title: Detached HEAD
levels.objective: HEAD is pointing at an old commit instead of a branch. Get back onto main.
hints: Switching to a branch reattaches HEAD.
levels.successMessage: "Detached HEAD" just means you were looking at a commit directly. Switching to a branch fixes it.
